Below is a summary of what’s happening and two small patches to fix it.

1) Bug scenario  
The screenshots show that a C++ literal like  
```cpp
auto i = 1'048'576;
```  
is being split up into a number (`1`), then a string (`'048'`), then another number (`576`). That happens because the C-style “string” rule in clike.js grabs anything in single quotes, and our current number regex doesn’t allow `'` as a digit separator.

2) Root cause  
Both in clike.js and in prism-c.js the `/number/` patterns only match plain digits (and hex digits), not `'` separators. We need to expand both regexes so that anywhere we match “\d” or “[0-9a-f]” we instead match “[\d']” or “[0-9a-f']”, including in exponents.

3) The patches  
Below are two `*SEARCH/REPLACE*` edits—one for `components/prism-clike.js` and one for `components/prism-c.js`. Each replaces the old number-regex with an enhanced one that allows single-quote separators.

```javascript
### components/prism-clike.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'number': /\b0x[\da-f]+\b|(?:\b\d+\.?\d*|\B\.\d+)(?:e[+-]?\d+)?/i,
    'operator': /--?|\+\+?|!=?=?|<=?|>=?|==?=?|&&?|\|\|?|\?|[-+*/~^%]/,
    'punctuation': /[{}\[\];(),.:]/
=======
    'number': /(?:\b0x[\da-f']+\b|(?:\b[\d']+\.?[\d']*|\B\.[\d']+)(?:e[+-]?[\d']+)?)/i,
    'operator': /--?|\+\+?|!=?=?|<=?|>=?|==?=?|&&?|\|\|?|\?|[-+*/~^%]/,
    'punctuation': /[{}\[\];(),.:]/
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

```javascript
### components/prism-c.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'operator': />>=?|<<=?|->|([-+&|:])\1|[?:~]|[-+*/%&|^!=<>]=?/,
    'number': /(?:\b0x(?:[\da-f]+\.?[\da-f]*|\.[\da-f]+)(?:p[+-]?\d+)?|(?:\b\d+\.?\d*|\B\.\d+)(?:e[+-]?\d+)?)[ful]*/i
});
=======
    'operator': />>=?|<<=?|->|([-+&|:])\1|[?:~]|[-+*/%&|^!=<>]=?/,
    'number': /(?:\b0x(?:[\da-f']+\.?[\da-f']*|\.[\da-f']+)(?:p[+-]?[\d']+)?|(?:\b[\d']+\.?[\d']*|\B\.[\d']+)(?:e[+-]?[\d']+)?)[ful]*/i
});
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

With these two changes, single‐quote separators in both integer and floating-point literals (including hex and binary exponents) will be correctly tokenized as one big “number” rather than broken into strings plus numbers.
